title: From Photographs to Free Knowledge: Inside Azad Reads’ Wikimedia Commons Workshop in Prayagraj
content:
A photograph can preserve a moment, its happiness and joy. But when that photograph is freely licensed, properly documented,machine readable and shared with the world, it can become part of something much larger than the person who took it.

That was one of the ideas that stayed with me after Azad Frames: Wikimedia Commons Essentials, a community workshop organised by Azad Reads in Prayagraj on 16 August 2026.

The workshop brought together photographers, readers, community members, and people who were simply curious about Wikimedia Commons and its wider Wikimedia eco-system.. For many participants, it was an introduction to the idea that contributing to Wikimedia does not necessarily begin with writing a Wikipedia article. Sometimes, it begins with a photograph already sitting in your phone.

Azad Reads is a Prayagraj-based community focused on reading, learning, and creating spaces for people to exchange ideas. The community has also been in documenting local heritage and building a repository of knowledge around Prayagraj.

This made Wikimedia Commons a natural point of connection.

title: The EduWiki Hub Starter Kit Arrives in Spanish
content:
The EduWiki Hub’s Newcomer’s Starter Kit, the education movement’s guide to teaching and learning with Wikimedia, is now available in Spanish. The translation was done by Patricia Aguilar, a Wikimedian from Mexico.

The Starter Kit was first launched in May 2026 during a multilingual orientation session with participants from across the movement. It was built to help educators, learners, and volunteers turn open knowledge into practice, combining practical guidance with community context.

Aguilar’s translation makes the kit available to Spanish-speaking educators and organizers, removing the need to use it in a second language.

The Spanish edition can support:

  • Onboarding volunteers and educators, with guidance on bringing Wikipedia into classrooms and lessons.
  • Program planning, as a reference for organizers designing workshops, setting metrics, and aligning with Wikimedia’s community standards.
  • Community management, with guidance for coordinators building welcoming, inclusive, and safe spaces for newcomers.

title: Wikimedia Foundation Bulletin 2026 Issue 16
content:
Here is a quick overview of highlights from the Wikimedia Foundation since our last issue on August 15. Previous editions of this bulletin are on Meta. Let foundationbulletin@wikimedia.org know if you have any feedback or suggestions for improvement!

  • Simplifying account creation: The Special:CreateAccount page has been simplified as part of ongoing work to modernize the account creation experience. Multiple account creation experiments show that a simpler form helps newcomers complete registration.
  • Movement Ecosystem strategy: Deadline to provide feedback on the first version of the proposal are extended until Sep 30 to allow more time for community feedback and discussion.
  • New format for the Community Wishlist: You can read the proposed ideas on Meta. This new process plans to improve how wishes are triaged, voted on, and prioritized in a way that is transparent and balanced across project families and language editions. Please let us know what you think will work well or if there are ways to make this proposal stronger. This consultation is open for two weeks.

title: EduWiki Hub OERs (April–July 2026): Growing Open Resources for Better Teaching
content:
Between April and July 2026, the EduWiki Hub saw steady growth in its library of Open Educational Resources (OERs), fueled by the ongoing work of dedicated educators, affiliate groups, and community volunteers around the world. Together, they contributed a fresh wave of instructional guides, grading tools, and outreach booklets designed to support Wikimedia-focused teaching in classrooms and training sessions alike.

This latest round of additions highlights 13 rich contributions in Czech, English, Indonesian, Malay, and Spanish, serving as a reminder of how global and multilingual the Wikimedia education community truly is. The new materials showcase resources on digital literacy, critical thinking, research skills, fact-checking and citation, and project management from a wide network of community groups and organizations, including Creative Commons Indonesia, EduWiki Hub itself, Wiki Education Foundation, Wikimedia Argentina, Wikimedia Czech Republic, Wikimedia Indonesia, Wikimedia México, Wikimedia UK, and WikiMelayu.

title: Bridging Access: Mapping Maternal and Child Health Facilities in Ikwerre LGA, Rivers State
content:
Access to reliable health information does not begin and end in a hospital. Sometimes, it begins with simply knowing where a health facility is, what it looks like, and that it exists. In Ikwerre Local Government Area (LGA) of Rivers State, Nigeria, maternal and child health facilities play an important role in providing essential healthcare to women, children, and families. Yet, information about many of these facilities remains poorly documented and difficult to find online.

This gap inspired “Bridging Access: Mapping Maternal and Child Health Facilities in Ikwerre LGA, Rivers State,” a Wikimedia project designed to make local health facilities more visible through photography, structured data, and community participation. The project brought together Wikimedia contributors and participants to document maternal and child health facilities across Ikwerre LGA and contribute this information to Wikimedia Commons and Wikidata.

title: Wikidata #2 workshop held in Tokyo, Japan
content:
We held a workshop about Wikidata in the Tokyo Metropolitan Library in Meguro district on August 22nd. This was the second event related to Wikidata organized by the Wikimedians of Japan User Group. 21 people have participated, comprising a diverse group of residents of both the Kansai and Kanto regions, ranging from beginners to experienced veteran editors.

This workshop was spearheaded by a member of Open Knowledge Japan forum Higashi Shusaku. First he explained what Wikidata is and how to edit it, then we continued into a hands-on practical session. Following a pre-prepared list of incomplete or missing entries, we all dove into the editing process.

We were joined by some truly inspiring people, including Eugene Ormandy, a Wikimedian of the Year 2023 nominee, and Hijiri, this year’s Honorable Mention nominee. Seeing that even such experienced editors still have things to learn was a huge motivation for the rest of us to keep learning.

title: The Yurakaré people and the Wikimedia movement
content: For a few years now, Wikimedistas de Bolivia has been working with representatives of Indigenous nations to put together open educational resources about the different languages spoken in the country. This year, the Bolivian user group got in touch with the Institute of Language and Culture of the Yurakaré Nation (ILC-NY) and invited its members to create an illustrated alphabet of their language and upload it to Wikimedia Commons. What we’d like is for Commons to eventually have open educational resources for all of Bolivia’s languages, available for anyone to download and use freely. That said, reaching out to the institutions in charge of safeguarding Indigenous languages in the country isn’t always straightforward, and it usually takes a long time.

title: Coordinate Me – The World’s Largest Wikidata Competition
content:
The third edition of the international Wikidata competition Coordinate Me 2026 has concluded with remarkable results, setting new records for community engagement and data enrichment on the platform. The circumstances remain unchanged from previous years: the competition was organized by Wikimedia Österreich and ran throughout May 2026 and brought together Wikidata editors from around the globe to improve and create geolocatable content.

The 2026 edition proved to be the most successful yet, with participants editing over 1 million items, setting yet another record for the competition after last year’s successful second edition. What makes this achievement particularly noteworthy is that 719 newly registered users joined the platform specifically for this event. This significant influx of newcomers was supported by introductory workshops in multiple languages, four of which were organized by Wikimedia Österreich, ensuring that new editors received proper guidance rather than being left to navigate the complexities of Wikidata alone, thus increasing the likelihood of newcomer retention.

title: A Week to Remember: Bridges Across Borders at WikiCamp 2026
content:
Summer International Youth WikiCamp 2026—perhaps this title alone is enough to convey the immense work, energy, and dedication poured into just seven days. Yet, this post is about more than just the accomplished work. It is about friendship, structure, responsibility, and, of course, the endless possibilities of Wiki.

During this WikiCamp, I—Argam Hakobyan—served as a Wiki-аssistant. For those who might not know what a Wiki-аssistant is, let me explain briefly. At WikiCamp, participants are usually divided into four or five groups, each with its dedicated Wiki-аssistant. The assistant’s main role is to guide participants during editing workshops, help them navigate article editing, correct mistakes, and review their progress. This is arguably one of the most responsible roles at the camp, as the participants’ progress and final outcomes depend heavily on the assistant’s support.

title: FY25-26 Annual Funding Programs Reflections & Learnings
content:
Every year, the Community Resources team shares reflections and learnings from our primary community funding programs: Rapid and General Support Funds. Our goal in sharing these reflections is to highlight and celebrate the volunteers and affiliates who sustain our movement, and to provide clear visibility into how our funding is being used. Read on for a transparent look at our FY27 grants budget, our priorities for the year, and the renewal of our grants strategy.

Over the 2025–2026 funding year, we supported 427 grants totalling $17.73 million across 90 countries, with 56.2% of funds distributed outside North America and Northern & Western Europe. Facing global economic turbulence, inflation, and volatile currency shifts, our Regional Funding Committees leaned into fiscal discipline while continuing to champion equity; growing active multi-year commitments to 47 and pushing decision-making closer to the communities through localised funding models like the Nigeria National Funding Initiative, CEE Rapid Fund Program, Wiki in Africa Campaigns, and the Wikimedia Colombia Hacerwiki 2026.

title: Wikimedia Residencies at UTDT: A WIR Experience from an Educational Program
content:
The WMAR education program is carrying out its first initiative to support Wikimedians in Residence (WIR). In this post, we will tell you about this initiative and how it is progressing.

The role of the WIR is widely recognized within the Wikimedia Movement, especially within GLAM programs or institutions. A Wikimedian in Residence (WIR) is a person who serves as a liaison between the institution to which they belong (museum, library, university) and the local Wikimedia chapter in their country. In this link, the WIR’s role is to implement open knowledge projects within the institution, such as digitization efforts, research, talks, or editing workshops.

title: 1Lib1Ref 2026 Campaign in Nigeria
content:
The 2026 edition of the #1Lib1RefNG campaign was held from 1 June to 30 June 2026 by Wikimedia User Group Nigeria as part of the global #1Lib1Ref (One Librarian, One Reference) initiative. The campaign aimed to improve the quality, reliability, and verifiability of Wikipedia by encouraging librarians, Wikimedians, and knowledge enthusiasts across Nigeria to add missing citations to Wikipedia articles.This year’s campaign combined a nationwide editing contest with community-led edit-a-thons, complemented by virtual and in-person training sessions that equipped both new and experienced contributors with the skills needed to make impactful contributions.

Virtual Office Hour

A virtual office hour was held on 13 June 2026 to onboard new participants, provide editing guidance, and respond to questions about the campaign. The interactive session helped participants understand how to identify citation gaps and contribute effectively to Wikipedia.

title: Wikipedia as an Educational Tool in Achachicala
content: It’s common to hear phrases like, “But that’s not serious—that’s from Wikipedia,” in educational communities or academic settings. Although virtually all of us have used Wikipedia at some point—often to begin a research project—we rarely acknowledge it or cite it in our bibliographies. We know that students use it to do their homework and that even artificial intelligence relies on it as one of its main sources of information, yet we still fail to fully recognize its value as an educational tool. Objectively speaking, however, it is a very powerful educational tool. That’s why, to me, recognizing that value is, at the very least, only fair.

title: Wiki Loves Mingachevir: Turkic Wikimedians United in Azerbaijan
content:
From August 12 to 16, Mingachevir hosted Wikimedians from across the Turkic world. The five-day Wiki Loves Mingachevir camp brought together members of the Azerbaijani Wikimedia community and international participants to share their experiences, learn from each other, and work on Wikimedia projects together.

The camp was organized by the Azerbaijani Wikimedians User Group with the support of the Ministry of Youth and Sports of the Republic of Azerbaijan and sponsored by Azersun Holding. The event was held as part of the celebrations for Wikipedia’s 25th anniversary.

I was part of the organizing team together with A.Aida88 and NurAy. One of our main goals was to create an environment where participants could learn from one another and spend time together beyond their usual online interactions.

Throughout the camp, participants took part in workshops, community presentations, edit-a-thons, team activities, and discussions about the future of Wikimedia. With contributors from five countries working and spending time together, Mingachevir became a place for Wikimedia communities to connect beyond their usual online collaboration.
